introduction: At this foundational level, we tackle the highly repetitive daily-life mathematical applications: Time & Work, Speed-Distance-Time, and Percentages. Mastery here relies entirely on avoiding long fractional calculations and using LCM shortcuts.

core_concepts.title: Time & Work (The LCM Method)
core_concepts.description:
Instead of using traditional fractions ($1/x$), assume the 'Total Work' to be the LCM (Least Common Multiple) of the given days.
- If A does a job in 10 days and B in 15 days, Total Work = 30 units (LCM of 10 and 15).
- A's Efficiency = 3 units/day, B's Efficiency = 2 units/day. Together they do 5 units/day.
- Total time together = 30 / 5 = 6 days.

core_concepts.title: Relative Speed Concepts
core_concepts.description:
When two moving bodies (like trains) travel simultaneously:
1. **Opposite Directions:** Their relative speeds are strictly added ($S_1 + S_2$).
2. **Same Direction:** Their relative speeds are subtracted ($S_1 - S_2$).
Note: The distance covered by a train crossing a stationary pole or a standing man is exactly equal to the train's own length.

core_concepts.title: Percentages, Profit & Loss
core_concepts.description:
Always identify the strict 'Base' value. 
- Profit or Loss percentages are ALWAYS calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless explicitly stated otherwise.
- Discount percentage is ALWAYS calculated strictly on the Marked Price (MP).

important_entities.name: Successive Percentage Change
important_entities.significance: If a value undergoes two consecutive percentage changes of $a\%$ and $b\%$, the net effective percentage change is perfectly given by: **$a + b + \frac{ab}{100}$**. (Use a positive sign for increments/profits and a negative sign for decrements/discounts).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Biggest Exam Trap: 'If A's salary is 25% more than B's, by what percentage is B's salary less than A's?' Students quickly answer 25%, which is mathematically incorrect. The base has changed from B to A. The correct answer is **20%** (Shortcut Formula: $\frac{R}{100+R} \times 100$).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: If a person travels at speed $S_1$ and reaches $t_1$ minutes late, and travels at $S_2$ reaching $t_2$ minutes early, the exact distance is: $\frac{S_1 \times S_2}{S_2 - S_1} \times \text{Time Difference}$.

exam_strategy_tips: A patent SSC JE and Banking tip: Solve 'Pipes and Cisterns' problems using the exact same LCM method as Time & Work, just treat the efficiency of the emptying (leak) pipe as a negative value.
